name: Should I choose a sliding or hinged shower door for a tight bathroom layout?

mainEntity.name: Should I choose a sliding or hinged shower door for a tight bathroom layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sliding glass doors run on a top track and slide parallel to the wall, making them ideal when a swinging door would bump into an adjacent toilet, vanity, or towel bar. However, sliding systems usually open only halfway, creating a narrower entrance to the shower stall. Hinged doors provide a wider entrance and a minimalist look, but they require ample clearance outside the enclosure so the glass does not hit fixtures. Your floor plan’s exterior clearance determines which design functions best.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sliding doors save space in tight layouts, while hinged doors offer a wider walk-in entry if exterior swing clearance allows.
